note: Finding links in a text nobody typed (spec/translation-file/finding.md). `terms` are the lines of the file that carry the term mark; the index is built from them once. A term is a candidate only if the SOURCE cites it (its key, at word edges, the longest first, never overlapping); its writings are then looked for in the text; ONE occurrence is a link (by A), none or several is none; a link a person set is kept when its exact words (`own` first) are found once, and named in not_found otherwise. Word edges: WordGlue. Nothing is ever rewritten.

in.writings: [{words, form}] — the term's word first (form null), then its forms in the ordinal order of their ids, then any candidate
in.claimed: [[start, end]] | absent — the passages already linked

written_in.out: [{writing, start, end, case}] — every place, in reading order; writing = position in `writings`; case = upper-first | lower-first | null

in.others: [{key, writings}] — the other terms the same source cites

written_among.out: [{writing, start, end, case}] — the places THIS term wins, in reading order

writings_of.out: [{words, form}] — its word (form null), then its forms in the ordinal order of their ids

in.unlinked: [key] | absent — the terms the line of those words refuses

cited_whole.out: the key of the term the words ARE the citation of (one place, all the words), or null

in.terms: [key] — the keys of the terms (an index of KEYS: what a source cites)
in.unlinked: [key] | absent — the terms the line refuses

cites.out: [{term, start, end}] — where the source cites a term, in reading order, UTF-16 units [start, end)
